supersedes: nothing. This is the FIRST anchor for hardware_class dev1-slo-v1, and the numbers in docs/bench/adr-051-baseline-dev1.json may NOT be read into it. That predecessor was measured with the Redis fleet on the colima-db Docker daemon — the same VM as the 3.6M-row EODHD corpus and unrelated testcontainer churn. dev1-slo-v1 runs the fleet on a dedicated 4 vCPU / 4 GiB colima-slo profile on internal storage, with nothing else permitted on that daemon. A different measurement plane is a different question.
caveat:
Recorded on the self-hosted Actions runner with the load generator CO-LOCATED with the proxy on the same cores. It is a REGRESSION anchor and states no capacity; config/performance-surface.toml declares this class slo_declarable = false for that reason.

BOX STATE, stated because it bounds what these numbers are worth, and it is materially better than the predecessor's. The host reservation drained an ordinary job on the OTHER runner application before measuring, quiescence was established over 140.1s of sustained load1/load5/load15 below 0.20/0.25/0.30 of 14 cpus, and the exclusivity assertion recorded zero non-owner ACTIVE records, zero macOS Runner.Worker processes and zero Runner.Worker processes inside the colima VM — the last of which no macOS process scan can establish. problems: [].

The tail is still the loose half: the six reps span p99 17,343-29,772us (+/-26%) while throughput spans 15,369.9-16,836.0 (+/-4.5%). So the throughput floor is a tight regression band and a tail regression smaller than that spread will not be caught here.
